question: What is the total full-time strength of personnels in the National Human Rights Commission, India?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Chairperson and five members**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The National Human Rights Commission (NHRC) of India consists of a **Chairperson and five full-time members**.
 
• The Chairperson is typically a retired Chief Justice of India, ensuring the highest level of judicial oversight in human rights matters.
 
• The five members include **four full-time members** and one ex-officio member who serves as the Chairperson of the National Commission for Scheduled Castes, Scheduled Tribes, Minorities, and Women.
 
• The NHRC was established on **12 October 1993** under the Protection of Human Rights Act, 1993.
 
• It aims to protect and promote human rights in India, including rights related to life, liberty, equality, and dignity of individuals.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Human Rights:**

 
 
• Human rights are fundamental rights that protect the dignity and freedom of individuals.
 
• They include rights such as freedom of speech, equality before the law, and protection against discrimination.
 
 
 
• **Protection of Human Rights Act, 1993:**
 
 
• This act provides for the establishment of the NHRC and State Human Rights Commissions (SHRCs).
 
• It outlines the powers and functions of the NHRC, including investigating human rights violations and recommending corrective measures.
 
 
 
• **Functions of NHRC:**
 
 
• Investigating complaints of human rights violations.
 
• Conducting inquiries, recommending reforms, and promoting awareness of human rights.
 
• It also reviews acts that may result in the violation of human rights and suggests remedies.
 
 
 
• **Composition of NHRC:**
 
 
• Chairperson: A retired Chief Justice of India.
 
• Four full-time members: Including individuals with judicial and human rights expertise.
 
• Ex-officio members from relevant commissions representing vulnerable sections of society.
